newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen down on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen down on Tuesday.

text.p: Polish shares fell for the ninth consecutive session and analysts said the stronger selling after price-fixing signalled the main market should fall in profit-taking at least one more time before a possible rebound.
"The falls could end after Tuesday with the market then waiting for further signals," said Bogdan Kornacki, a trader at Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) brokerage.

Analysts said one such signal could be whether the two parties in the ruling coalition agreed on tax rates for next year after the lower house of parliament's surprise vote last Thursday cutting taxes for low earners.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 2.6 percent to 13,149.0 and turnover inched up two percent to 94.8 million zlotys on both markets.

Some analysts saw more falls after any brief rebound, saying investors would continue to take profits after the main market had risen about 100 percent this year to its October 9 high of 15,078 points.

"The market could end the year around 11,000 points, which would be a significant rise of about 50 percent from the start of the year," said Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital & Investment.

Analysts said the news that food prices rose only 0.2 percent in the second ten days of September would likely have little influence on the market since the central bank had said no interest-rate cut was imminent.
They said the low turnover of loss leader Bytom suggested the scale of its 9.9-percent fall was accidental.
Continuous trade turnover was at 1.1 million zlotys with biggest mover Budimex down 3.5 percent. NFI units fell 4.8 percent in the regular session and fell 5.3 percent in 30-million-zloty live trade.
